jobTitle: Engineer, Product Design and Engineering – Mechanical
jobDescription:
Driving Innovation in Power Transmission Design?

Do you enjoy transforming engineering concepts into real-world industrial solutions?

Partner with the best

Baker Hughes stands as a leading global energy technology company, delivering innovative solutions that make energy safer, cleaner, and more efficient across the entire value chain. Operating in more than 120 countries, the company blends deep industrial expertise with advanced engineering and digital technologies to support energy production, transformation, and decarbonization. With over a century of heritage, Baker Hughes partners with customers in oil and gas, industrial sectors, and emerging energy markets to accelerate progress toward a more sustainable energy future.

Fuel your passion

The Engineer, Product Design and Engineering – Mechanical is driving the execution of new and duplicate power transmission projects by applying strong mechanical engineering principles, analytical skills, and cross-functional collaboration. The role is contributing to the design, evaluation, and delivery of industrial power transmission products while ensuring compliance with technical standards and supporting both manufacturing teams and customers with technical expertise.

As an Engineer, Product Design and Engineering – Mechanical, you will be responsible for:


  • Executing design, analysis, and evaluation activities for assigned power transmission projects while adhering to industry regulations and internal standards.
  • Applying engineering principles, calculations, and methods to design a wide range of industrial power transmission products across multiple industries.
  • Developing new power transmission solutions under guidance, in team settings, or based on engineering design precedents.
  • Collaborating with fellow engineers and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless project execution.
  • Communicating project deadlines, technical needs, risks, and presenting engineering outcomes effectively.
  • Delivering engineering designs and bills of materials on time and with high quality as part of a cross-functional team.
  • Supporting manufacturing teams during product build phases to ensure design intent is met.
  • Assisting customers with technical expertise and addressing project-related questions.


To be successful in this role you will:


  • Have a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from an accredited institution.
  • Have authorization to work in the US without sponsorship.
  • Have excellent working knowledge of 3D modeling software; Creo experience is a plus.
  • Have strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills.
  • Have strong verbal and written communication abilities.
  • Have proven analytical and critical thinking capability.
  • Have the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering and business functions.
  • Have experience working with gears (preferred).


Work in a way that works for you

We recognize that everyone is different and that the way in which people want to work and deliver at their best varies. In this role, we can offer the following flexible working patterns:


  • Working flexible hours — adjusting your schedule to support productivity and personal needs.


Working with us

Our people are at the heart of what we do at Baker Hughes. We know we are better when all our people are developed, engaged, and able to bring their whole authentic selves to work. We invest in the health and well-being of our workforce, train and reward talent, and develop leaders at all levels to bring out the best in each other.

Working for you

Our inventions have revolutionized energy for over a century. To continue shaping the future, we reward those who embrace change with a package that reflects how much we value their contribution. You can expect:


  • Contemporary work-life balance policies and wellbeing activities
  • Comprehensive private medical care options
  • Safety net of life insurance and disability programs
  • Tailored financial programs
  • Additional elected or voluntary benefits


You will be eligible to participate in Company-sponsored benefit programs, including health & welfare programs and the Thrift Plan (401k). You will have a choice of coverage options that best suit your needs. Coverage options and contribution amounts are related to your benefit elections, base salary level, and specific requirements of each of these plans.

This position is eligible for our comprehensive and competitive benefits package, which can be found here, and is further eligible for additional forms of compensation such as bonuses subject to the terms of the applicable benefit plans or policies.

The Baker Hughes internal title for this role is: Engineer 2, Mechanical, Product Design and Engineering

About Us:

We are an energy technology company that provides solutions to energy and industrial customers worldwide. Built on a century of experience and conducting business in over 120 countries, our innovative technologies and services are taking energy forward – making it safer, cleaner and more efficient for people and the planet.

Join Us:

Are you seeking an opportunity to make a real difference in a company that values innovation and progress? Join us and become part of a team of people who will challenge and inspire you! Let’s come together and take energy forward.

jobTitle: Mechanical Design Engineer II - Mechanical Systems
jobDescription:
Job Description

Honeywell is launching the development of a new family of gas turbine engines that will help shape the future of the aerospace industry. Honeywell is hiring engineers in the areas of design, analysis, controls, test, and project management to accomplish this challenging new feat. We are looking to hire individuals who thrive on thinking big, have an appetite for growth, and a passion for winning.

You will report directly to our Mechanical Engineering Manager, and you’ll work out of our Phoenix, AZ location on a Hybrid work schedule.

Honeywell has an opening for an engineer in the Mechanical Systems Engineering group responsible for the design and analysis of bearings, gears and splines, seals, and lubrications systems for propulsion engines, auxiliary power units and engine gearboxes. The scope of this position includes using state-of-the-art software tools and methods and supporting Technical Excellence Teams to capture and publish analysis practices and guidelines. The position may involve test rig design, operation, and data collection and analysis. Analytical results may be presented in design reviews and will be recorded in appropriate documentation to meet program deliverables and requirements. Applicant must work effectively with design teams, global support, and chief engineers.

Responsibilities

  • Design and develop mechanical systems, components, and assemblies in accordance with project requirements.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define mechanical requirements and specifications.
  • Perform mechanical analysis and simulations to ensure product performance and reliability.
  • Document and present analytical results in design reviews and technical reports.

Qualifications

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Must have a Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering.
  • Due to ITAR requirements, must be a US Citizen or Legal U.S. Permanent Resident Alien (Green Card Holder)
  • Minimum 2 years of engineering experience in turbine engines or electric motor/generator applications

WE VALUE

  • Understanding and application of disciplines in high speed machinery for one or more of these areas:
    • Bearings
    • Gears & splines
    • Air & oil seals
    • Lubrication systems
  • Familiarity with mechanical systems for gas turbine engines or electric motors / generators
  • Strong oral, written and persuasive communication skills are required to interact with engineering teams and other disciplines.
  • Ability to work with multidisciplinary teams to meet expectations of internal customers.
  • Under minimal supervision, ensure that tasks are appropriately defined, supported, and achieved in a timely manner.
  • Ability to juggle many priorities and competing demands easily and effectively
Benefits

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/

U.s. Person Requirements

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

About Honeywell Aerospace

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

About The Business Unit

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com

Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep aircraft flying. With engines across roughly 120 aircraft types and more than 47,000 APUs in service today, we support operators across commercial and defense markets — backed by an aftermarket network built for the long service life of every platform we power.

We continually invest in our employees and provide training and tools for advancement, development, and career progression—whether you prefer a path to become a subject matter or technical expert, a people leader, a project manager, or a leader in business development. Another day, you may be leading a valve replacement project, evaluating equipment options, or preparing technical reports such as corrosion studies or evaluations of equipment options.

  • Deliver High-Quality Engineering Documents: Prepare accurate and error-free drawings, sketches, calculations, and analyses that meet industry codes, standards, and regulations, ensuring client needs are met with precision

Are you a Mechanical Engineer, passionate about fitness, and looking to gain hands-on experience and grow your skills? Life Fitness / Hammer Strength is looking for a Mechanical Engineer II to join our team. You'll be part of a team responsible for the design, analysis, and release of components and assemblies used in industry-leading cardio and strength fitness equipment, from concept through production launch. The role is ideal for a candidate with strong CAD skills, particularly in SolidWorks, and a willingness to learn and grow in part design and product development. The engineer will also support existing products by assisting in resolving field, service, and manufacturing issues as needed.

This is a hybrid role based out of our manufacturing facility in Ramsey, MN. M/F remote and T-Th are in-office collaboration days.

As a Mechanical Engineer at Life Fitness / Hammer Strength, you will:

  • Conceptualize, design and document components and systems consisting of sheet metal, castings, structural tubing, plastic and electromechanical components using SolidWorks design software.
  • Perform engineering analyses, such as Finite Element Analysis (FEA), dynamic simulations, design calculations, and tolerance analysis, to prove out the feasibility of component and sub-system designs.
  • Work with the product development team to develop product specifications and timelines.
  • Work with reliability and compliance teams to develop component and product test plans.
  • Collaborate with other engineering disciplines, Product Management, manufacturing, purchasing and document control departments within Life Fitness as well as outside customers and vendors.
  • Ensure product and component designs meet aesthetic, reliability, cost, manufacturability and regulatory requirements.
  • Develop and procure prototype parts and build prototype units.
  • Develop and release production Bills of Materials (BOM's)
  • Lead projects to improve Mechanical Engineering department processes and procedures, as assigned.
  • Follow Life Fitness Mechanical Engineering departmental procedures and design guidelines to complete engineering tasks as assigned.
  • Travel up to approximately 20% to support supplier visits, prototyping, and production activities
  • Mentor others within the department

What Life Fitness / Hammer Strength is looking for in our Mechanical Engineer:

  • Bachelors of Science in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent, required
  • 3+ years of experience as a mechanical engineer in a related field
  • Efficient with 3D CAD software, SolidWorks preferred
  • Good understanding of drawing development and drafting standards.
  • Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) preferred
  • Good understanding of BOM development/management
  • Capable of completing engineering analyses, such as: FEA, heat transfer, dynamic simulation, various hand calculations
  • Good knowledge of metal part design, including: sheet metal, weldments, castings, machined components, aluminum extrusions
  • Good knowledge of plastic component design, preferred, including: injection molding, extrusions, thermoforming
  • Knowledge of electromechanical component design/application, preferred
  • Working knowledge of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools, such as Teamcenter preferred
  • Working knowledge of Design for Six Sigma (DFSS) tools preferred
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent presentation skills
  • Strong interpersonal skills for working with external and internal teams
  • Demonstrated indirect leadership experience in professional or volunteer organizations preferred

A U.S. citizen;

Job Description

The Systems / Mechanical Engineer will serve as a technical lead and subject matter expert supporting the evaluation, definition, design, manufacture, and verification of complex mechanical systems, including nuclear and other high‑consequence applications. This role supports both commercial and U.S. Government customers and emphasizes end‑to‑end lifecycle execution—from requirements development through manufacture, test, and validation.

The position includes responsibilities in systems engineering, mechanical design, thermal and structural analysis, engineering trade studies, subsystem integration, and close collaboration with manufacturing and quality organizations. The engineer will employ Model‑Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) as a disciplined approach to capturing, decomposing, and managing requirements, defining system architectures and interfaces, and maintaining end‑to‑end traceability across the product lifecycle.

The engineer will develop, manage, and decompose system and subsystem requirements; establish verification and validation requirements using Test, Analysis, Demonstration, and Inspection (TADI) methods; and prepare design and procurement specifications. The role also includes preparing technical presentations; conducting system requirements reviews, design reviews, manufacturing readiness reviews, and test readiness reviews; and briefing customers, senior and mid‑level leadership, and cross‑functional stakeholders.

The successful candidate will be capable of clearly communicating technical concepts and program status to engineering, manufacturing, test, quality assurance, and business office personnel, and of presenting well‑reasoned technical recommendations to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Bachelor’s degree in an accredited engineering discipline (Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related field)
  • 5–12 years of relevant experience in systems engineering and/or mechanical engineering supporting complex hardware programs
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, manage, and decompose system and subsystem requirements
  • Experience developing and managing verification and validation requirements, including TADI (Test, Analysis, Demonstration, and Inspection) methods
  • Experience preparing and reviewing design specifications and procurement specifications
  • Ability to prepare technical presentations and conduct system requirements, design, manufacturing readiness, and test readiness reviews
  • Experience briefing customers, senior and mid‑level leadership, and cross‑functional teams
  • Experience supporting regulated, safety‑critical, or high‑consequence engineering programs
  • Strong background in Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and/or Design for Assembly (DFA)
  • Experience working directly with engineering, manufacturing, test, quality assurance, and suppliers
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work across multidisciplinary teams
  • Experience supporting commercial and/or U.S. Government customer programs

  • Experience with ASME codes and/or NQA‑1 quality programs is a strong plus, but not a requirement
  • Experience using MBSE tools such as Cameo Systems Modeler (plus)
  • Experience with software/control system/Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) requirement development and/or design (plus)
  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license (plus)

Engineers in this role support products including Torchmate®, Vernon Tool®, MasterPipe®, PythonX®, and Linc-Cut™, while also collaborating with teams across Lincoln Electric Automation on a variety of robotic, welding, and industrial automation projects.

 

This position is ideal for a motivated engineer who enjoys hands-on involvement in machine design, industrial automation, robotics, and new product development and is looking to expand their technical expertise across a diverse portfolio of automation products.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

 

  • Design and develop mechanical systems, assemblies, and components for automation equipment and products.
  • Design machine structures, motion systems, cutting process equipment, and related electromechanical assemblies.
  • Develop and maintain 3D CAD models, engineering drawings, bills of materials, and product documentation in accordance with company standards and revision control processes.
  • Apply engineering principles, calculations, simulations, and analytical methods to support design decisions.
  • Support and Execute product development projects throughout the lifecycle, from concept and design through validation, manufacturing release, and product support.
  • Develop and execute product validation and verification activities, analyze performance data, investigate technical issues, and implement design improvements to enhance product reliability, quality, safety, and manufacturability.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing teams to support prototype builds, production implementation, and Design for Manufacturability (DFM) reviews.
  • Coordinate and collaborate with electrical, controls, software, manufacturing, and service teams to develop integrated automation solutions.
  • Provide technical support to production, service, and quality departments as required.
  • Maintain compliance with company safety policies and applicable industry standards.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education and Experience

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering.
  • 2+ years of experience in mechanical design, product development, machine design, automation, or industrial equipment.
  • Proficiency in creating 3D CAD models, detailed engineering drawings, and bills of materials.
  • Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, including mechanics, materials, and manufacturing processes.
  • Strong mechanical design, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with industrial automation, robotics, CNC equipment, welding systems, motion control, or custom machinery.
  • Familiarity with fabrication, machining, welding, assembly, and manufacturing processes.
  • Proficiency with Solid Edge, SolidWorks, or similar CAD platforms.
  • Experience with Product Data Management (PDM) systems and revision control processes.
  • Experience supporting product testing, validation, or commissioning activities.
  • Familiarity with electromechanical systems including motors, drives, sensors, pneumatics, and industrial controls.
  • Hands-on experience working in manufacturing, prototype, or laboratory environments.

Physical Demand and Work Environment

  • Primarily office-based engineering environment with frequent interaction in manufacturing and prototype assembly areas.
  • Occasional lifting of equipment, tools, or components up to 25 pounds.
  • Regular use of computers, engineering software, and standard office equipment.
  • Occasional standing, walking, bending, and working around manufacturing equipment.
  • Exposure to manufacturing environments may include noise, moving machinery, welding operations, and varying temperatures.
  • Occasional travel may be required to support product development, testing, installation, or customer-related activities.

About the Team

Compute & Connectivity Hardware (CCH) is part of GM's Vehicle Software & Electronics Engineering (VSEE) organization within Software & Services Engineering. Our team develops the hardware foundation that powers GM's software-defined vehicles, including compute platforms, connectivity systems, networking architectures, displays, and other electronic technologies that enable infotainment, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), vehicle controls, and connected customer experiences.


From concept through production, CCH engineers drive architecture, requirements development, electronics design, hardware integration, validation, launch, and in-market performance. We partner closely with software, systems, cybersecurity, functional safety, manufacturing, suppliers, and vehicle engineering teams to deliver reliable, scalable hardware solutions across GM's global vehicle portfolio.


About the Role

We are seeking a Mechanical & Thermal Engineering Technician to support the development, testing, and validation of in-house electronics designs (IHED) and next-generation vehicle technologies. This hands-on role is responsible for test setup, instrumentation, data collection, and execution of mechanical, thermal, and environmental testing of electronic modules and components.


The successful candidate will work closely with Mechanical, Thermal, and Electrical Engineering teams to execute test plans with high quality and repeatability, enabling data-driven engineering decisions and product validation.


Key Responsibilities

Test Setup & Execution

  • Prepare and execute mechanical, thermal, and environmental tests on electronic modules, PCBs, and enclosures, including thermal characterization, vibration, mechanical shock, thermal cycling, and thermal shock testing.
  • Set up fixtures, mounting hardware, and test configurations according to engineering requirements, drawings, and test procedures.
  • Operate laboratory equipment including environmental chambers, vibration shakers, thermal chambers, wind tunnels, power supplies, and data acquisition systems.
  • Perform pre-test and post-test functional verification and document test observations, issues, or anomalies.

Instrumentation & Data Acquisition

  • Install and configure thermocouples, strain gauges, accelerometers, displacement sensors, and other instrumentation.
  • Route and secure wiring and sensor connections to ensure reliable data collection and test integrity.
  • Monitor and record temperature, strain, acceleration, and other performance metrics using data acquisition systems.
  • Support calibration activities and verify instrumentation compliance with laboratory standards and procedures.

Data Collection & Reporting

  • Capture, organize, and maintain test data, photographs, setup documentation, and supporting records.
  • Conduct basic data validation and trend analysis to identify anomalies and summarize findings for engineering teams.
  • Assist in the creation of standardized test reports by compiling data, observations, and test results.

Laboratory Operations

  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organized laboratory environment in accordance with GM safety requirements and established 5S practices.
  • Support equipment maintenance, calibration coordination, troubleshooting, and readiness activities.
  • Manage inventory of test fixtures, tooling, instrumentation, and consumable materials.
  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on testing efficiency, documentation quality, and workflow optimization.

Collaboration

  • Partner with Mechanical, Thermal, and Electrical Engineers to understand test objectives, requirements, and constraints.
  • Communicate test progress, risks, and technical issues in a timely manner.
  • Participate in test planning reviews, readiness assessments, and engineering discussions.

Basic Qualifications

  • Associate degree, technical certification, or equivalent experience in Mechanical, Electrical, or Mechatronics Technology.
  • 5+ years of experience in an engineering, electronics, thermal, or validation lab.
  • Experience with thermal, environmental, vibration, and shock testing.
  • Ability to read engineering drawings and test procedures.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, especially Excel.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and safety focus.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with automotive electronics, PCBs, or electronic control modules.
  • Hands-on experience with thermocouples, strain gauges, accelerometers, and DAQ systems.
  • Familiarity with thermal management and validation testing.
  • Experience in automotive, aerospace, or similar product development environments.
  • Strong communication, troubleshooting, and multitasking skills.

Work Location

This position is primarily on-site and requires regular presence within the Mechanical & Thermal Engineering Laboratory to support hardware preparation, test execution, equipment operation, and hands-on engineering validation activities.

Job Description: Mechanical Engineer

A Mechanical Engineer at United Science develops manufacturing processes by studying product requirements;

researching, designing, modifying, and testing specifications and manufacturing methods and equipment.

Duties and Responsibilities of Mechanical Engineer

• Work on product development or sustaining projects, which involve design, replacement or redesign for

obsolete components, product improvement features, cost reduction, manufacturing support, and field

complaints.

• Prepare assembly or product layout and detailed drawings, and participate in the manufacture or building of

prototype product or system.

• Provide tolerances studies, apply GD&T, conduct stress-analysis studies, develop reliability testing

procedures, and generates appropriate design verification reports.

• Design testing methods to analyze product capabilities and troubleshoot any mechanical or structural flaws.

Perform analysis tests to track results and make improvements.

• Recommend design changes, cost reductions, warranty improvements, and manufacturing issues.

• Work with marketing and vendors, providing product specifications for their use.

• Ensure that design implementation, test, and maintenance methods/processes are developed and executed in

a manner that supports company quality standards.

• Write product specifications, document test results, prepare product operating instructions and review

technical literature.

• Participate in test runs or field installations.

• Participate in scheduled department meetings to report progress of overall project or portion of project, and

prepare and give design presentations, and mentor junior engineers and technicians.

Mechanical Engineer Skills and Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology

• Strong ability with computer-aided design systems and experience with mathematical computing and analysis

tools knowledge (SolidWorks, AutoCad, PDM).

• Superior computer skills; well-versed in Microsoft Office Suite (particularly strong with Excel);

• Able to create 2-D or 3-D designs to run simulations, analyze, and tests

JOB TITLE: Mechanical Designer

EFFECTIVE DATE: 11/04/2021

DEPARTMENT: Engineering

SUMMARY OF FUNCTIONS:

The Mechanical Designer uses computer aided design and development (CADD) techniques to prepare

drawings, diagrams, illustrations and schematics for product documentation/literature and all types of

publications according to company and regulatory specifications and standards.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Proficiently utilizing CAD software for drafting and illustrating including three-dimensional

perspectives of documentation to satisfy documentation requirements for Engineering,

Manufacturing, Marketing and Customer Service.

• Renders new product concept illustrations from free-hand sketches or marketing or engineering

input. Makes suggestions to product committee on various design requirements and

recommends possible solutions or alternate constructions. Prepares evaluations of strength of

materials, tolerances and stresses, weights and cubed dimensions.

• Prepares new or improved product and component documents for engineering and

manufacturing including layouts, blueprints, assembly and detail drawings. This can also include

development of drawings for special tools, fixtures, process and test equipment.

• Creates product or component illustrations including block diagrams, schematics, isometric

illustrations, orthographic illustrations and three-dimensional perspective illustrations for use in

marketing literature, manuals and sales video presentations.

• Creates exploded-view drawings for operation, service and assembly manuals from product and

component detail drawings and bill of materials in accordance with operating/set-up

instructions or assembly/disassembly breakdowns.

• Provides other drafting and illustrating services as needed by engineering, production, customer

service or as requested by the management.

ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS:

Reports directly to the CEO. Coordinates activities with Engineers, Designers, Marketing,

Production, and Customer Service Departments.

QUALIFICATIONS:

A college degree is preferred with a major in graphics design preferred. Good communication skills and

the ability to work well with people is essential. Familiarity with computer design software is required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Ability to communicate orally with customers, management, and other co-workers is crucial. Regular use

of the telephone and e-mail for communication is essential. Sitting for extended periods is common.

Hearing and vision within normal ranges is essential for normal conversations, to receive ordinary

information and to prepare or inspect documents.

No heavy lifting is expected. Exertion of up to 10 lbs. of force occasionally may be required. Good

manual dexterity for the use of common office equipment such as computer terminals, printers,

scanners, copiers, and FAX machines.

Good reasoning ability is required to solve a wide range of graphics problems. Able to apply geometry,

algebra and other analytics as required. Able to understand and utilize graphics designs, illustrations,

and engineering drawings to conduct business.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The job is performed indoors in a traditional office setting. Activities include extended periods

of sitting and extensive work at a computer monitor.

Job Summary

Nidec is the world's No. 1 comprehensive motor manufacturer handling "everything that spins and moves", miniature to gigantic. Nidec is a global enterprise comprised of over 300 subsidiaries/affiliates. We are a leading manufacturer of commercial motors, industrial motors, appliance motors, and controls. Our product line features a full line of high efficiency motors for industrial applications in water treatment, mining, oil and gas, and power generation, and for commercial applications such as pool and spa, condensers, cooling towers and large refrigeration units.

From keeping us comfortable in our homes to pumping clean water to making our cars more safe, electric motors are an indispensable part of our daily lives. At Nidec, our employees are on the forefront of developing new motor technologies. As we move deeper into the age of robotics, the impact of motors will only increase.

With over 140,000 employees stationed worldwide, Nidec continues to be a unique organization, and each location maintains its individual personality.

Whether driving locomotives, powering offshore platforms or keeping the lights on after a storm, Nidec electric power generation products impact the world on a daily basis. With over 1,000 employees in the Americas, we are moving forward with technology to solve our customers' electrical power needs for both prime and backup generation needs as the industry's leading manufacturer.

Position Objective:

Research, plan, and design mechanical and electromechanical products and systems and direct and coordinate activities involved in fabrication, operation, application, installation, and repair of mechanical or electromechanical products and systems by performing the following duties. 

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

  • With Direct Supervision:

    • Perform calculations using math tools including but not limited to Excel, MathCad, and Xlrotor

    • Conduct finite element structural analysis. 

    • Evaluate field installations and recommend design modifications to eliminate machine or system malfunctions.

    • Research and analyze customer design requirements, specifications, manuals, and other data to evaluate the feasibility, cost, and product maintenance.

    • Work with sales to research and analyze customer specifications to create design proposals.

    • Create detailed designs for manufacturing in a cross functional environment following manufacturability and quality initiatives.

    • Review drawing packages and order documentation completed by other designers and engineers.

    • Design Products, applying engineering principles to meet customer specifications.

    • Design products to meet safety, industry, and agency certification requirements.

    • Evaluate project requirements for required effort and provide estimated completion times. 

    • Evaluate design projects to ensure the latest design practices are being utilized.

    • Perform testing to evaluate structural, thermal, and vibration of products.

    • Create bills of materials and assist designers/technicians with the creation of bills of material.

    • Coordinate assembly and testing activities to ensure products and systems conform to engineering design and customer specifications.

    • Work closely with production during construction of initial machine release to record and improve manufacturing or procurement challenges.

    • Evaluate customer test requirements and assign existing or write new test procedures to meet requirements.

    • Presents proposed designs to customer and help negotiate changes required to eliminate functional or dimensional problems

  • Without Direct Supervision:

    • Maintenance and support of existing products to include reliability, cost, and manufacturability product improvements. 

    • Assign GD&T dimensional tolerance on parts and check tolerance stack up.

    • Communicate product specifications to electrical and mechanical designers and provide guidance on how the specifications affect product design.

    • Other Activities as directed by management.

    • Document and clearly communicate technical results within company and customers as appropriate.

Experience/Skills:

  • Knowledge of AC or DC synchronous / inductive motors and generators.

  • Experience with rotating equipment and generators.

  • Product design and development experience in structural and mechanical machinery.

  • Able to organize, prioritize, and complete responsibilities in a timely manner without external motivation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. 

  • Demonstrated initiative, organizational skill, and professional work habits

  • Able to quickly achieve and maintain a high degree of trust and confidence

  • Experience with engineering tools to perform calculations and analysis (Includes but not limited to Excel, MathCAD).

  • Proficient in PTC Creo or Similar 3D Modeling Software 

  • Experience in AutoCAD

  • Proficient with GD&T

  • Ability to clearly and effectively communicate with other departments inside the organization as well as with customers.

  • Proficient with the use of various software applications, including but not limited to: Oracle (ERP), Aras (PLM), Adobe Acrobat, and Microsoft Office

  • 0-3 years’ work experience minimum in structural and mechanical machinery product design.

  • Must be a US Citizen for positions at the North Mankato facility.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering

Job Summary

A rapidly growing division of Nidec Motor Corporation seeks candidates to fill an Engineer IV position, in St. Louis, MO. Nidec is the world's leading manufacturer of small precision motors, including motors used in hard disk drives and optical disk drives (including Blu-ray disk drives). The company has extended its focus beyond the information storage motor market to the industrial, home appliance, and automotive markets, where it sees high future growth potential. Nidec Motor Corporation is primarily engaged in the manufacture and sale of industrial and high efficiency motors in applications ranging from water treatment, mining, oil and gas, power generation, air conditioning, rooftop cooling towers and commercial refrigeration. Manufacturing facilities and technology centers are located in the United States, Mexico, China, India, and the UK.

Duties

  • Serve as design engineer for equipment, fixtures, and tooling, required to support re-manufacture of heavy wheeled and tracked vehicles and associated sub-assemblies.
  • Perform complex engineering duties associated with the conception, design, redesign or modification of equipment, fixtures and/or tooling to support maintenance mission programs.

Qualifications

This announcement has been extended until 9/25/2026.

Who May Apply: US Citizens

In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). Basic Requirement All Professional Engineering Positions:
A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics;(d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR
B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.
2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.
3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program.
4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you MUST ALSO meet the qualification requirements listed below:

GS-05 Basic Qualifications: Applicants who meet the basic requirements described in the individual occupational requirements are fully qualified for the specified entry grade of GS-05.

GS-07 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level or higher equivalency in the Federal service which includes work that involves:
1) Applying a basic understanding mechanical engineering theories, concepts, principles, and methods to all phases of mechanical systems design and computations;
2) Assisting in the preparation of engineering designs; and
3) Assisting in the inspection of engineering projects.
OR
Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: engineering technology, physics, or chemistry.
OR
Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:
1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses; OR
(2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum.; OR
3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/).
OR
Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages.

GS-12 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or higher equivalency in the Federal service which includes work that involves:
1) Preparing engineering designs for equipment, fixtures, and tooling required to support tracked vehicles.
2) Inspecting engineering projects for conformity with plans and specifications; and
3) Reviewing engineering drawings, plans and specification or cost estimates for engineering projects.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11 or above) Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.

Duties

  • You will serve as the team leader for assigned system safety program, managing the identification, analysis, documentation, and correction of system safety hazards
  • You will develop system safety risk assessments in close collaboration with relevant engineering subject matter experts and facilitate risk acceptance by the appropriate authority.
  • You will provide review of Engineering Change Proposals, Fleet Technical Publications, and evaluate Flight Clearances to ensure hazards are identified, communicated and that the appropriate hazard controls are in place
  • You will prepare correspondence, technical reports, cost estimates for project funding, fact sheets, status reports and schedules as required to complete project assignments.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • Must be a US Citizen.
  • Must be determined suitable for federal employment.
  • Must participate in the direct deposit pay program.
  • New employees to the Department of the Navy will be required to successfully pass the E-Verify employment verification check. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, visit e-verify.gov
  • Generally, current federal employees applying for GS jobs must serve at least one year at the next lower grade level. This requirement is called time-in-grade. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.
  • Within the Department of Defense (DoD), the appointment of retired military members within 180 days immediately following retirement date to a civilian position is subject to the provisions of 5 United States Code 3326.
  • Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service.
  • You will be required to obtain and maintain an interim and/or final security clearance prior to entrance on duty. Failure to obtain and maintain the required level of clearance may result in the withdrawal of a job offer or removal.
  • This position is covered under the Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA). Certification in the Acquisition Functional Area and category assigned to the position is required within established category timeframes.
  • This position may require travel from normal duty station to CONUS and OCONUS and may include remote or isolated sites. You must be able to travel on military and commercial aircraft for extended periods of time.

Qualifications

Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the DP-03 (GS-9/11) grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: professional MECHANICAL ENGINEER, performing some or all of the following duties:
1) Developing and processing System Safety Risk Assessments (SSRA) for risk acceptance, which include recommendations for economical and efficient engineering mitigations. Developing detailed technical safety analyses for highly complex systems to include considerations for hardware failures, software faults, and human factors behaviors.
2) Developing tailored system safety programs based on customer requirements and Navy, DOW and other government agency policies. Managing and directing safety program as the technical authority to ensure progress toward requirement completion within budget and schedule constraints. Developing clear and thoughtful contractual language for obligating safety program tasking and deliverables as required to contractor partners.
3) Serving as a system safety team leader, coordinating with internal, external, and government engineering disciplines to document and resolve system safety hazards and ensure safety-minded design features are considered during both design and mitigation program phases. Acting as chair for System Safety Working Group (SSWG) discussions to facilitate/resolve identified hazards.
4) Serving as a technical consultant and expert for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, the Laser Safety Review Board and the Weapon System Explosive Safety Review Board for cognizant systems assigned. Provides review of Engineering Change Proposals, Naval Air Training and Operating Procedures Standardization, evaluates Flight Clearances and other programmatic products and functions to ensure hazards are identified, communicated and appropriate hazard controls are in place.
5) Preparing detailed cost estimates for use in obtaining project funding. Preparing correspondence, technical reports, briefing material and presentations, fact sheets, status reports and schedules as required to complete project assignments.

https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series AND https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0800/files/all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Education

Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual:

Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position.

OR

Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org

OR

Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html.

OR

Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above)

OR

Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

jobDescription:
Purpose  

The Mechanical Engineer supports Morgan City engineering activities for both small and large projects, as well as individual components of complex projects within Oceaneering's Subsea Robotics (SSR) and Offshore Projects Group (OPG). Typical work scopes include, but are not limited to, Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs), Intervention Workover Control Systems (IWOCS), ROV Workover Control Systems (RWOCS), ROV tooling, survey systems, installation and light construction projects, diving operations, inspection, maintenance, and repair (IMR) activities, and other assignments as directed by the Engineering Team Lead or Engineering Manager.

The Mechanical Engineer is responsible for supporting the full product and project lifecycle, including concept development, detailed design, engineering analysis, manufacturing support, testing, offshore operations, and field support. Key responsibilities include developing and reviewing engineering deliverables, performing calculations and analyses, conducting design reviews, supporting manufacturing and supply chain activities, troubleshooting technical issues and ensuring compliance with client requirements, applicable industry standards, and Oceaneering policies and procedures.

.

Work Location and Travel

  • Role provides the opportunity to work in hybrid environment, working both virtually and in office when required.

  • Position may require some travel including internationally and offshore.

  • Ability to travel offshore up to 20% of the time.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL

  • Ensure engineering activities are conducted in accordance with Oceaneering policies, processes, and safety requirements, with a strong focus on personnel and environmental safety. 

  • Ensure engineering deliverables comply with client requirements, contract specifications, and applicable industry standards including ISO, API, ANSI, DNV, AWS, and other relevant codes. 

  • Perform conceptual and detailed mechanical design, engineering analysis, and design verification for subsea equipment, tools, and systems. 

  • Design mechanical systems and equipment that interface with ROVs, subsea hardware, and related offshore systems. 

  • Develop and review engineering calculations, design packages, manufacturing drawings, assembly drawings, system layouts, and technical documentation. 

  • Prepare and review engineering specifications, procedures, work instructions, test procedures, user manuals, and related technical documents. 

  • Evaluate existing designs and implement improvements related to performance, reliability, manufacturability, safety, and cost. 

  • Select appropriate materials, coatings, cathodic protection systems, and corrosion mitigation solutions for subsea applications. 

  • Design pressure-containing and pressure-tolerant equipment, including systems requiring multiple electrical, hydraulic, or mechanical penetrations. 

  • Support engineering projects, technical proposals, bids, and project execution activities. 

  • Develop engineering cost estimates, schedules, work scopes, and progress reports. 

  • Communicate project status, technical issues, risks, and recommendations to customers, project teams, and management. 

  • Participate in internal and external design reviews and provide technical recommendations. 

  • Evaluate equipment, components, and suppliers and support technical sourcing and supplier qualification activities. 

  • Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, service, supply chain, project management, and field personnel to support successful project execution. 

  • Provide technical support for manufacturing, assembly, testing, troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair activities. 

  • Develop and execute test programs for factory acceptance testing (FAT), system integration testing (SIT), qualification testing, certification testing, and field trials. 

  • Attend and support FAT, SIT, offshore trials, commissioning activities, and customer demonstrations as required. 

  • Perform technical evaluations, root cause investigations, and corrective action development for field and operational issues. 

  • Support engineering change management, configuration control, and continuous improvement initiatives. 

  • Prepare and deliver technical presentations and training to internal and external stakeholders. 

  • Provide on-site oversight of subcontractors, offshore operations, installations, commissioning, and field support activities when required. 

  • Travel domestically and internationally, including offshore assignments, to support project execution, testing, commissioning, and customer requirements.

  • Participate in design risk assessments, FMEA reviews, and hazard analyses.

  • Support transition of new products into manufacturing through testing, documentation, training, and readiness activities.

 

Supervisory Responsibilities

 

This position has no supervisory responsibilities

 

Reporting Relationship

 

  • Reports to the Engineering Team Lead / Manager. 

 

Qualifications

REQUIRED

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Mechanical) or other related field. 

  • Minimum of two (2) years of engineering experience.

  • Must be able to obtain:

    • Transportation Workers Identification Card (TWIC)

    • Petroleum Education Council (PEC) Basic Training

    • Basic Offshore Safety Induction and Emergency Training (BOSIET)

 

DESIRED

  • Knowledge of GD&T, tolerance stack up analysis, and design for manufacturability 

  • Knowledge of ROV and/or subsea equipment design and engineering

  • Knowledge of basic hydraulic components and the ablity to read hydraulic schematics and P&IDs 

  • Working knowledge of Solidworks, AutoCAD, MathCAD, and ANSYS 

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

  • Good communication and presentation skills

 

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Characteristics

 

  • Ability to work in a team environment, remaining attentive to ideas, recognizing responsibilities, and actively participating with others to accomplish assignments and achieve desired goals.

  • Ability to write reports, business correspondence, procedures, and manuals. 

  • Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. 

  • Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

  • Gives and receives constructive feedback.

  • Ensures that others involved in a project or effort are kept informed about developments and plans.

  • Ensures that regular consistent communication takes place within area of responsibility.

 

Working Conditions

 

This position is considered 80% OFFICE WORK which is characterized as follows. 

  • Almost exclusively indoors during the day and occasionally at night.

  • Occasional exposure to airborne dust in the work place.

  • Work surface is stable (flat).

  • May, on occasion be sent out to the equipment yard (local or otherwise) or machine shop to participate in the assembly, FAT, or SIT of projects or other functions as needed.

 

This position is considered 20% OFFSHORE WORK which is characterized as follows.

  • Outdoors and indoors, day and night, as well as over/near water.

  • Requires work on or newar moving equipment and vibrating equipment

  • Frequently the humidity is above 90%, noise is over 85 decibels and the light is intense/glare

  • Potential exposure to open fire/flames/sparks

  • Constant exposure to airborne dust, fusmes, and gases

  • Work surface is stable, height is elevated

 

Physical Activity/Requirements

This position is considered LIGHT work.

Overview

As a Mechanical Engineer, you will provide mechanical and plumbing engineering expertise to support project design, construction, and delivery. You will work closely with internal teams, clients, consultants, architects, and contractors to develop effective solutions that meet project requirements, applicable codes and standards, and Kitchell’s commitment to quality.

This position will support a variety of projects and will be responsible for providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle, from design development and documentation through construction administration and closeout.   • Support the development of technical approaches, scopes of work, and fee estimates for assigned projects.
  • Assist with proposals, presentations, and other technical marketing materials as requested.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with clients, consultants, contractors, and internal teams.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to less experienced engineering staff as appropriate.
  • Stay current with applicable building codes, regulations, industry standards, and emerging mechanical engineering practices.

Requirements

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university in mechanical engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience required.
  • 5+ years of relevant mechanical engineering experience preferred.

Techtronic Industries, the world leader in cordless technology across Outdoor Power Equipment, Power Tools, Floor Care Appliances, and Accessories, is seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer for the Ryobi Outdoor Products Advanced Engineering team at our Innovation Center in Anderson, SC.

This role is ideal for a hands-on mechanical engineer who enjoys turning ambiguous product ideas into working, tested, manufacturable solutions before they enter formal product development. You will help develop future outdoor power equipment technologies by converting early concepts into validated mechanical systems that improve performance, durability, user experience, and manufacturability.


Advanced Engineering operates upstream of traditional new product development. The team explores new mechanisms, proves out key technical assumptions, reduces risk through analysis, prototyping, and testing, and transitions mature concepts to product development teams.

The Advanced Engineering team is highly collaborative, deeply hands-on, and driven by curiosity, learning, and practical problem solving as we develop innovative outdoor products that create real value for our customers.

  • Define system requirements, user operation methods, design trade-offs, and acceptance criteria for advanced mechanical systems
  • Translate early concepts into robust, production-minded designs that can be handed off to downstream engineering teams
  • Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Industrial Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and other cross-functional teams to develop balanced technical solutions

  • Experience building prototypes, developing test plans, evaluating results, and using data to improve designs

  • Experience with rapid prototyping across multiple materials and processes
  • Familiarity with vibration, sound, airflow, thermal, durability, or performance testing
  • Familiarity with integrated electrical and mechanical systems, including motors, batteries, sensors, and control interfaces
  • Advanced degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

Tools & Technologies:
Candidates should be comfortable using modern engineering tools to develop, analyze, communicate, and validate mechanical designs.

Summary

The Mechanical Engineer designs, specifies, and validates the mechanical hardware and systems the plant runs on. This covers custom fabrication and change parts, modifications to existing equipment, conveyance and material handling, machine guarding, drive systems, and the mechanical utilities that support production.

Where the Manufacturing Engineer defines how a product is made, this role defines the physical means of making it and is accountable for whether that hardware is sound, sanitary, serviceable, and safe. A design that runs but cannot be cleaned, cannot be maintained, or cannot be reproduced from the drawing has not met the standard.

Duties and Responsibilities

Mechanical Design and Fabrication

•      Produce three dimensional models and detailed fabrication drawings for change parts, tooling, fixtures, guards, transitions, chutes, hoppers, frames, and platforms, with tolerances and finishes specified rather than left to the fabricator.

•      Perform the engineering calculations that support a design, including loads, stress, deflection, fatigue, torque, drive sizing, and power transmission selection.

•      Select materials and finishes appropriate to a food environment, accounting for product contact, cleaning chemistry, temperature, corrosion, and wear.

•      Apply sanitary design principles to all custom fabrication, including radii, surface finish, drainability, avoidance of crevices and hollow bodies, and appropriate fastener and joint selection.

•      Manage fabrication through internal shop resources and outside vendors, including drawing release, quoting, progress review, inspection, and acceptance of finished work.

•      Maintain drawing control, revision history, and bills of material so a part can be reordered years later without being reverse engineered.

Equipment Modification and Machine Systems

•      Design and validate modifications to existing production equipment, and assess the effect of any modification on machine safety, sanitary status, warranty, and original equipment manufacturer support before it is made.

•      Design and lay out conveyance and material handling systems, including transfers, accumulation, elevation changes, and product handling that protects product integrity.

•      Size and select drive components including motors, gear reducers, belts, chains, bearings, and couplings, and document the basis of selection.

•      Design machine guarding and access to the applicable safety standard, and support machine safety risk assessments.

•      Design pneumatic and hydraulic circuits and specify components for the application and the environment.

•      Design for maintainability, so that wear parts can be reached, serviced, and replaced without disassembling unrelated equipment.

Mechanical Utilities and Facility Systems

•      Provide engineering support for mechanical utility systems including refrigeration, steam and condensate, compressed air, process water, wastewater, and heating and ventilation.

•      Perform load, capacity, and sizing calculations for utility systems and distribution, and identify where capacity constrains production or where a system is oversized and wasteful.

•      Specify piping, valves, pumps, and heat transfer equipment appropriate to the service, including sanitary service where product contact applies.

•      Support Process Safety Management activities where ammonia refrigeration is present, including process hazard analysis, mechanical integrity, and management of change.

Asset Integrity and Reliability Engineering

•      Analyze mechanical component failures to determine the mechanism, including wear, fatigue, misalignment, lubrication, overload, or material selection, and correct the design or specification rather than reordering the same part.

•      Specify predictive and condition monitoring strategy for mechanical assets, including vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis, and alignment standards.

•      Engineer the critical spare parts strategy, including interchangeability, standardization across equipment and across sites, and identification of single source risk.

•      Assess equipment condition and remaining life, and develop replacement and rebuild recommendations with a supporting technical and financial case.

Standards, Documentation, and Technical Support

•      Develop and maintain mechanical engineering standards for design, materials, fasteners, guarding, and documentation, so work is consistent across projects and across sites.

•      Maintain accurate mechanical documentation including assembly drawings, part drawings, layouts, and equipment files.

•      Provide engineering support to Maintenance on mechanical problems that exceed routine repair, and to Manufacturing Engineering on the hardware requirements of process and capital work.

•      Support internal, customer, regulatory, and third party audits by producing design documentation and technical justification on request.

•      Provide technical direction to designers, drafters, fabricators, and outside vendors, and verify their work against the specification.

•      Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

Required

•      Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent demonstrated design engineering capability and experience.

•      Three or more years of mechanical design experience in a manufacturing environment.

•      Demonstrated proficiency in three dimensional computer aided design and in producing complete, dimensioned, buildable fabrication drawings.

•      Working knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, fits, and surface finish specification.

•      Ability to perform and document the engineering calculations that justify a design, and to state the assumptions behind them.

•      Working knowledge of materials, coatings, and elastomers suitable for food contact and washdown service.

•      Working knowledge of power transmission and drive component selection.

•      Working knowledge of machine safety standards, guarding design, and risk assessment.

•      Ability to work with fabrication shops and vendors, including reading their constraints back into the design.

•      Willingness to be present on the floor and on off shifts during installation, trials, and startup, since a design is proven at the machine and not at the desk.

Preferred

•      Experience with SolidWorks.

•      Familiarity with 3-A Sanitary Standards and with ASME BPE requirements.

•      Experience with ammonia refrigeration systems and Process Safety Management requirements.

•      Vibration analysis, alignment, or other predictive maintenance certification or training.

•      Working knowledge of welding and fabrication processes sufficient to design for the shop that will build it.

•      Familiarity with applicable pressure piping and pressure vessel codes.

•      Professional Engineer license, or progress toward it.

•      Bilingual in English and Spanish.

Expectations and Measures of Success

Performance in this role is measured by whether the hardware works, holds up, and can be lived with. The following describe what success looks like.

•      Designs install and run as intended, without field rework to make them fit or function.

•      Custom fabrication cleans, drains, and passes sanitation and audit scrutiny.

•      Drawings and bills of material are complete and current, so parts can be reordered or rebuilt from the documentation alone.

•      Mechanical failures are analyzed and designed out rather than replaced repeatedly.

•      Spare parts complexity decreases over time through standardization across equipment and across sites.

•      Maintenance regards the designs as serviceable, which is a judgment they make and not one this role can assert.

Supervisory Responsibility

Typically none. This role provides technical direction to designers, drafters, fabrication shop personnel, vendors, and contractors without formal supervisory authority. Some sites may assign designers, engineering technicians, co ops, or interns to this position.

Work Environment

This role divides time between an office or design environment, the maintenance and fabrication shop, and the production floor of a food manufacturing facility. On the floor and in the shop, the employee is exposed to moving mechanical parts, welding and grinding operations, wet and slippery surfaces, cleaning chemicals, and loud noise requiring hearing protection, in refrigerated, ambient, or mixed temperature areas depending on the site. Time on the floor increases substantially during installation, trials, commissioning, and shutdowns. Presence on off shifts, weekends, and during planned shutdowns is expected, since installation work occurs outside of normal production hours.
